claims.content: The Customer wants to manage their account settings by updating and saving their membership account information, such as name, contact details, password, and email notification preferences.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to manage their account settings by updating and saving their membership account information, such as name, contact details, password, and email notification preferences.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer accesses the Manage Account Settings page, enters updated membership account information, and saves the changes successfully.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is on the Manage Account Settings / Change Membership Account Information screen and is ready to modify their settings.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has successfully saved the updated account settings.
in_scope_actions: Update membership account information fields (e.g., name, contact details, password)
excluded_adjacent_actions: Administrative site-wide global settings management (Auction Administration)
Downstream account administration or post-save processing outside this use case
variant_dimensions: Which account setting category is edited (contact fields vs. email notification preferences)

claims.content: Customer
The user has an existing membership account with registration information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail Address, Phone) and a current password already stored in the system.
The user is logged in to the system (authenticated), as indicated by a personalized welcome message.

The use case is triggered when the Customer accesses the 'My Account Edit Page' (specifically pages for editing Membership Information, Billing/Shipping Addresses, or Payment Methods) to update their stored account data.

The Customer views the 'My Current Information' section, which displays their existing First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address, and Phone, and requires entry of the Current Password to authorize changes.

The Customer enters updated information into the 'My New Information' section fields: First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address (entered twice for verification), Phone, and Password (entered twice for verification).
The Customer clicks the 'Save Changes' button to submit the updated membership account information.
The Customer is returned to the My Account page after the changes are saved.

Diverges from Step 3: Instead of clicking the 'Save Changes' button, the Customer clicks the red 'Cancel' button; any entered changes are discarded and the Customer is immediately returned to the My Account page without saving changes.

Diverges from Step 2: In the address editing section, the Customer may select the 'Same as Billing Address' checkbox to automatically populate the New Shipping Address fields with the billing address data, avoiding manual re-entry.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may click the 'Change my "Auction Insider" Email Newsletter Subscription' link to opt out of the 'Auction Insider' newsletter subscription instead of modifying email notification preferences on the current page.
Diverges from Step 2: If the Customer has chosen PayPal or Amazon as their payment type, the 'Please notify me when I win an auction' checkbox is grayed out so the Customer may not de-select the box.

At Step 1, if the Customer does not complete the required current-password authorization, the system prevents modification of the membership account information; the update attempt is blocked before any account changes are accepted.
At Step 2, if the Customer enters a password outside the required 8-to-12 character range, the system triggers a validation error and prevents the save.
At Step 2, if the two password fields contain mismatched values, the system rejects the save through the password-validation failure path.
At Step 3, when the E-mail Address is verified during save, if a duplicate email is found in the customer table, the system treats the submission as an error condition requiring correction.
At Step 3, if the Member ID ('Handle') being saved is not unique in the database customer table, the system reports an error state.

At Step 3, if the Core web service returns address-correction suggestions for a new or edited address and the Customer does not accept them, the system may reject the address input as invalid or block/flag the save.

missing_aspects: Explicit retry/continuation behavior and error-message text after the listed validation rejections are not specified in the evidence.
Explicit confirmation that password mismatch triggers rejection (currently implied by UI structure rather than explicitly stated in source).

claims.content: The Customer's selected email notification preferences ('notify me when I am outbid', 'notify me when I win an auction', 'notify me when my winnings are shipped') are saved and will govern future transactional email behavior.
